short: A timed stretch of the match; each one ends with the bell and a break sheet where you give orders and draft a relic.
more: Later Acts open more jungle clearings and switch on pressure events, and from Act 7 the game pushes toward an ending.

short: The tolling that ends an Act: once the board is calm, play stops and the break sheet opens.
more: If a fight will not stop, the bell tolls anyway after about half a minute. Nothing is moved or reset while play stops.

short: Your team's spending meter (0–100): it fills over time and from kills, and pays for gambits and pawns.
more: It starts at 30 and gains 1 every second, plus bonuses for piece kills, pawn kills and Bastions. Full Tempo that sits unspent is wasted.

short: Your whole side: five pieces, their pawns and pawnlings, your Bastions and your Throne.
While your King is dead and your Throne still stands, your court is in Check: he respawns slower and your team deals 10% less damage.
more: Check is also the name of a gambit that marks an enemy piece so it takes extra damage for a few seconds.

short: The end of the match: a court loses the moment its Throne is down and its King is dead.
more: Either order counts. A Throne that has fallen also stops the King from ever respawning.

short: Pauses the match so you can move pieces between lanes, change build paths and read the Armory.
A lane tower that shoots enemies in range; each court has two in every lane, and destroying one earns Tempo.
more: Bastions take only half damage from pieces, so pawnlings and pawns do most of the pushing, and the Rook is built to break them.

short: Your base structure; it never moves, and once it falls your King can no longer come back from the dead.
more: Lose the Throne and the King together and the match is over: that is Checkmate.

short: A sunken wood beside a side lane that holds jungle camps; its pines block line of sight, and you enter through stone gates.
Standing on a higher tier than your target: your hits land 20% harder and ranged pieces reach 30% farther.
more: The Long Board has three tiers: the river is lowest, the midfield terrace is next, and each home terrace is highest. Hitting uphill is 20% weaker.

short: A small eye above a piece's health bar: it is hitting a target below it, so it hits 20% harder.
more: Ranged pieces with the eye also reach 30% farther. The badge stays up for at least two seconds so you have time to notice it.

short: Whether a piece can see and shoot a target: a grove's pines block sight and shots across its edge, except through gates and roads.
more: A piece with no line of sight walks round to an opening instead of shooting. The central Pit has no such rule.

short: A piece's level from 1 to 8, earned from the gold it collects; ranks grow its stats, and Ranks 4 and 8 bring a fork.
The style a piece chooses at Rank 4 from three options; it adds a fourth skill and tilts the piece's stats.
more: Until Rank 4 a piece uses its base kit. At Rank 8 it gets a smaller choice between two upgrades.

short: A choice a piece earns at Rank 4 (pick an archetype) and Rank 8 (pick one of two upgrades); play pauses until you choose.
more: Let the AI choose picks for you. The Knight's Fork gambit is a different thing: a leap that stuns one enemy piece.

short: Which items a piece buys first: Offense, Defense or Utility; pieces shop on their own.
more: Each piece starts on its natural path. The AI may add an armor or resist item against the enemy's damage.

short: An elite foot soldier you field with Tempo; it is much tougher than a pawnling and does not come back when it dies.
more: There is a cap on living pawns. Auto pawns field them for you in the lanes you choose at each break.

short: A small soldier that both courts send marching down every lane in waves; killing them earns gold.
A card you play with Tempo to give an order, such as pushing a lane, holding a file or marking an enemy piece.
more: You hold a hand of three. A card you do not play expires after a while and is replaced.

short: One of six families of gambits (March, Initiative, Fortress, Sacrifice, Position, Clock); each is strong against some and weak against others.
more: Counters work through card effects, never by cancelling a card: Fortress, for example, soaks a March push.

short: Your setup choice that tilts which gambit cards you are dealt; most favour two schools, doubling their chance.
more: The Italian Game is balanced and favours none. Black picks an Opening too, and you see it a little way into the match.

short: A permanent bonus your court drafts at each Act break: pick one of three, and hold up to three.
more: A relic takes effect from the next Act. Black drafts relics too, and its newest one stays hidden until that Act starts.

short: A kind of relic that works only while your court is behind when the break begins.
more: Closed Position, King's Ransom, Compensation and Sortie are Rally relics; whether they apply is read once, at the start of the break.

short: The Act break shop: each piece can buy and sell items with its own gold; Adjourn shows the same view, read only.
more: Untouched pieces shop on their own when you resume, and Black shops at every break too, though its new items stay hidden until the next Act starts.

short: The six items a piece buys, in order, when it shops on its own; it starts as the build path's list.
more: Change it at any Act break in the Armory. Changing the build path resets it to that path's list; a plan you changed stays yours at Rank 4.

short: A place in a piece's bag: it carries at most six items, and a full bag cannot buy until it sells one.
The smaller items a bigger one is made of; parts a piece already owns are used up and come off the price.
A brass pip on the item the AI would buy next for this piece; Let the AI shop buys by the same rule.
A top-tier item with a powerful effect; the Armory sells them at each Act break, and the jungle shops sell them during an Act.
